PullRequest.Title: Agents/remove automation prioritized notifications
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The one-item-to-one-provider-request call path and absence of an aggregate limiter are explicit. Only the exact typical item count is uncertain; model calls are intrinsically expensive enough that an unbounded cold-start burst is material.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Language-model provider IPC/network requests and concurrent streamed responses
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold service instance the loop schedules one request per distinct notification preview signature, including active and dismissed items; aggregate concurrency is therefore O(N) in the number of current notification items, with only per-signature deduplication and no global limit.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive concurrent network/IPC traffic, provider throttling, and reduced throughput for other language-model work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, notifications used their existing descriptions and this path made zero language-model requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A constructor autorun now eagerly calls ensurePreview for every item; every cache miss immediately invokes generatePreview, which independently calls sendChatRequest.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 420 creates the collection-wide eager loop; each iteration can reach the newly added sendChatRequest boundary, whereas the base revision had no preview generation.
Findings.Title: Bound preview generation instead of firing one model request per item
Findings.Impact: Restoring or receiving a batch of many sessions can launch tens or hundreds of utility-model calls at once while the Inbox is closed, consuming bandwidth/quota and delaying both previews and unrelated Copilot requests.
Findings.Evidence: The added autorun at lines 417-423 iterates allItems, explicitly including active and dismissed items. ensurePreview calls generatePreview immediately on every miss (line 440); generatePreview has only a Set keyed by signature, and invokePreviewModel delegates directly to the provider with sendChatRequest (lines 476-487). ILanguageModelsService.sendChatRequest itself directly delegates to provider.sendChatRequest (languageModels.ts:1461-1473), so there is no downstream global limiter established here.
Findings.Recommendation: Generate previews only for items needed by the visible Inbox (or a bounded prioritized subset), and route misses through a small shared limiter that drops/cancels stale signatures. Preserve the existing signature cache and per-key coalescing inside that bounded queue.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The map mutation sites and absence of eviction are exhaustive in repository search, and the allocation/retention scaling follows directly. Only the time needed for a user to accumulate a large H is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained preview keys/strings and repeatedly copied Map entries
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After H unique preview signatures over the workbench lifetime, retained state is O(H), and publishing the next result clones all H entries, making cumulative publication allocation O(H²); removed items and changed signatures are never deleted.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory plus increasing CPU/GC pressure as notification content churns.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The base service had no generated-preview map or retained preview history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every generated preview clones the entire observable map and appends the signature, but no lifecycle path removes signatures that are no longer present in allItems.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 448 copies the ever-growing published map on each new signature; both the map and this repeated-copy mechanism are introduced by the diff.
Findings.Title: Evict stale entries from the published preview map
Findings.Impact: Long-running workbenches with recurring session turns, PR state changes, or external notifications steadily retain obsolete previews; later preview completions become progressively more allocation-heavy despite the nominal 200-entry LRU.
Findings.Evidence: The service declares a bounded PREVIEW_CACHE_SIZE of 200 and an LRUCache at lines 288-292, but publishPreview creates `new Map(current)` at added line 448 and adds the new entry before publishing it. Repository search shows _previews is only initialized, read, and appended to (lines 312, 432, 444-450); there is no delete/clear synchronized with allItems. Thus the observable map bypasses the LRU bound and each insertion copies its entire retained history.
Findings.Recommendation: On allItems changes, retain only signatures still referenced by current items (optionally plus a truly bounded recent set), and publish a bounded snapshot; alternatively expose per-key observables backed directly by the existing LRU so obsolete signatures can be evicted without cloning retained history.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous pre-await call path and post-processing-only cap are directly visible. Session-history sizes vary, but long agent sessions are a realistic input and cost scales linearly with their full history.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread Markdown-to-plaintext CPU work and intermediate strings/arrays
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Selection cost grows with every markdown response part and total transcript bytes in the session, even though only 6,000 output characters are retained.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing click latency and potential UI jank when opening details for a long completed session.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the detail-summary feature, selecting a notification did not synchronously convert its full chat history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Detail generation synchronously walks the complete chat history, renders every markdown part to plaintext, joins all output, and only then truncates it to DETAIL_MAX_INPUT_CHARS.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 731 introduces per-part Markdown rendering on the selection call stack; the diff's nominal 6,000-character bound does not bound this work because it is checked only after all parts are processed.
Findings.Title: Apply the transcript cap before processing the whole history
Findings.Impact: Selecting a completed card from a long-running agent session can block the renderer while the entire transcript is converted and allocated before the loading state can remain responsive.
Findings.Evidence: renderCompletedEvidence calls requestDetailSummary synchronously from the selection render (view line 1415). The async generateDetailSummary performs getSessionTranscript before its first await (service lines 622-630). That helper traverses all requests and executes renderAsPlaintext at added line 731, then joins and normalizes the full accumulated transcript at line 734; the 6,000-character slice is applied only afterward at line 738.
Findings.Recommendation: Build the transcript incrementally and stop once the 6,000-character budget is satisfied (also bound oversized individual source parts before conversion where possible), then defer any remaining preparation off the immediate selection/render stack.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The delayed registration, new eager dependency, constructor autoruns, and concrete refresh/load calls are directly traced. Exact latency varies with session/PR count and provider speed, but the moved boundary fan-out is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub network refreshes and pollers plus chat-session load operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On every restored workbench, cost grows with non-archived sessions and their pull requests: the service launches up to three refresh/poll paths per open PR and one chat-model load per needs-input or unread-completed chat, without a shared limiter.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased post-restore network traffic, background CPU, and contention that can degrade startup responsiveness.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The singleton was registered with InstantiationType.Delayed and was reached only when the Inbox view or its accessible view was requested, so users who did not open Inbox paid none of its PR hydration, polling, or chat-load cost.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new AfterRestored contribution injects IInboxNotificationsService, forcing its previously delayed singleton to construct in every workbench and run all constructor autoruns even when the Inbox is never opened.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 98 registers an always-on AfterRestored contribution whose added constructor requires IInboxNotificationsService; before this diff there was no after-restore consumer forcing the delayed service to initialize.
Findings.Title: Keep full inbox hydration off the after-restore path
Findings.Impact: Starting VS Code with many agent sessions or PR-backed sessions now immediately fans out GitHub refreshes/startPolling calls and chat model loads in the background, even if the user never opens Inbox.
Findings.Evidence: inboxOne.contribution.ts:27 keeps the service delayed, but the added contribution registered here is instantiated AfterRestored and its constructor dependency at inboxNotificationsToast.ts:31 resolves that service. InboxNotificationsService's constructor then loops every session through ensureGitHubModels (lines 333-337); that method calls refresh and startPolling for PR, review-thread, and CI models (lines 864-907), while another constructor autorun calls acquireOrLoadSession for each relevant chat through line 1418. These are fire-and-forget loops with no aggregate limiter.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep toast detection lightweight: defer PR refresh/polling and chat-model hydration until the Inbox is shown, or split/gate the service so the toast path hydrates only a changed resource through a bounded shared limiter rather than initializing every session.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Selection-to-request reachability and missing cancellation are explicit. The number of rapid selections varies, which affects severity but not the concurrency mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Language-model provider IPC/network requests carrying up to 6,000 transcript characters each
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For cold entries, concurrency grows with the number K of completed cards selected before earlier generations finish; deduplication is only by item id, so K different selections produce K simultaneous requests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive model traffic and contention that delays the summary for the item the user is currently viewing.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: There was no completed-item detail pane or detail-summary model request before this change.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Rendering every newly selected completed item starts a detail-summary generation immediately; leaving that item disposes the UI but does not cancel its service-side request.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1415 puts a model-generation boundary on each completed-card selection; the base view had no selection-triggered model work.
Findings.Title: Cancel or serialize detail summaries when selection changes
Findings.Impact: A user browsing several completed notifications in quick succession can leave all prior 6k-character generations running while only the last result is useful, consuming network/provider capacity and slowing the selected detail.
Findings.Evidence: The added call at line 1415 runs on completed-item detail render. requestDetailSummary starts generateDetailSummary immediately for every uncached item (service lines 595-608), and invokeDetailModel sends a provider request (lines 647-676). Each request's CancellationTokenSource is placed in _previewCancellationSources (line 624), but that set is cancelled only when the whole service is disposed (lines 350-354), not when selection/detailDisposables change. There is no shared limiter across item ids.
Findings.Recommendation: Own the active detail request from the selected-item lifecycle: cancel the prior item's token when selection changes and/or serialize requests through a latest-selection-first limiter. Keep completed cached results, but do not continue cold requests for details no longer displayed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore with existing agent sessions while the Inbox is never opened
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution starts at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored, so these operations are not awaited by the nominal restore gate, but they begin immediately afterward and compete with interactive work, extensions, and other network/model activity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh PR metadata, review threads, and CI and start their polling
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three refresh/poll paths per open PR after model/state checks, across every non-archived session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The calls existed, but the delayed service was not instantiated for users who did not open Inbox/accessibility; the new AfterRestored toast contribution moves them onto every restored-workbench path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget after restore; does not gate restore completion but consumes network/provider/renderer resources during early interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load persisted chat sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced load per needs-input chat and per unread completed session main chat; aggregate launches are not globally limited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only occurred after the delayed Inbox service was requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous background loads compete with early interaction and I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send utility-model preview request and consume streamed response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per cold distinct current notification signature, including active and dismissed items; N requests can be concurrent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the restore gate, but an unbounded provider burst can throttle unrelated model work and consume bandwidth/quota.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Non-archived sessions, open pull requests attached to those sessions, needs-input/unread-completed chats, and effective notification items after grouping PR candidates by session/kind.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The constructor loops sessions synchronously and launches refresh/load promises without awaiting or a shared limiter. Preview generation independently launches one request per cold distinct signature; only duplicate signatures are coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub WeakSets prevent repeat refreshes for the same model object within one service lifetime; chat resource maps coalesce a resource while loaded. Preview caches are in-memory only, so restore is cold; successful signatures coalesce, but misses/failures have no negative cache and the published map never evicts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the AfterRestored dependency, delayed registration, constructor loops, and concrete boundary calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of sessions/PRs and provider latency varies by user, but users of background agents plausibly retain dozens of sessions and the boundary placement/cardinality is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff moves full-service hydration onto every restore and separately adds an unbounded per-item model-request burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: A batch of sessions or notification states changes while the Inbox is closed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Notification derivation and toast detection run immediately on the session/provider event. Preview responses are not needed to emit the toast, so model work is off the functional critical path but competes with ongoing user/model activity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke copilot-utility-small for a one-line preview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per effective cold signature in the batch, all concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Descriptions were rendered directly with zero language-model calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for the toast or notification's fallback description; purely eager background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective distinct preview signatures among all derived items after item-id grouping; unchanged signatures hit the in-memory map/in-flight set, changed signatures miss.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All cold signatures are started in the same autorun pass. There is per-signature in-flight deduplication but no aggregate limiter, queue, or backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm successful signatures avoid work. Changed content gets a new hash. Empty output, no-model results, and failures are not negatively cached and can retry on a later allItems invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: eager allItems iteration and direct provider delegation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical batch size is uncertain, but a provider/session refresh can expose many items together and each request is independently expensive.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: eager work and absent global concurrency control create avoidable boundary fan-out while the UI is closed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Inbox and selecting or browsing completed notification details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Card selection synchronously renders the detail. Before the first await in summary generation, the complete session transcript is converted to plaintext. The model response itself is asynchronous and gates the generated evidence pack, not basic view interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render every markdown response part to plaintext, join the full transcript, then truncate to 6,000 characters
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-history traversal per cold completed item selected; CPU/allocation grows with the entire history rather than the retained prefix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No selection detail or full-history conversion existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on selection before generateDetailSummary reaches its first await, directly increasing click latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a detail evidence-pack language-model request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold completed id selected; K rapidly browsed ids can leave K requests active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected generated evidence waits for this request; stale prior requests contend with it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total requests/markdown response parts and bytes in the selected session; for network concurrency, the number of different cold completed items selected before earlier requests finish.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Transcript conversion is serialized on the renderer click path. Detail requests are coalesced only by item id; requests for previously selected ids continue concurrently because selection disposal does not cancel their tokens.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm detail-summary key prevents another request and the service has a 50-entry LRU. The observable detail map is not itself evicted, and a cold selected id starts immediately. Failure publishes an empty fallback marker, acting as a per-id negative cache for the service lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous pre-await traversal and token lifetime through service disposal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most sessions are short, but long agent sessions and browsing several completed entries are realistic; exact jank/provider delay varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: full-history work defeats the input cap on the click path, and selection changes do not cancel expensive stale requests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Long-running workbench with recurring notification content changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preview publication is asynchronous, but every completion mutates an observable used by the visible cards; map copying and observer invalidation occur on each result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate each previously unseen preview before publication
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful call per unseen signature over time; warm current signatures avoid repeats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No generated preview boundary or retained preview state existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous; not required for fallback rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifetime count H of unique preview signatures from session turns, PR state changes, and external notification updates, including signatures no longer referenced by current items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests may complete concurrently, but JavaScript publications serialize; each publication copies the map containing all earlier retained signatures.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The declared LRU holds 200 entries, but the published _previews map is separate and has no delete/clear path, so it bypasses the intended bound.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all _previews mutation sites were inspected and no eviction exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Time to accumulate a large H depends on session churn, but retention and O(H) copy cost per insertion are unconditional once signatures accumulate.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the bounded LRU does not bound the authoritative observable map, causing lifetime memory growth and progressively heavier publication.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and full diff pagination. Submitted five diff-caused findings covering always-on hydration fan-out, unbounded preview concurrency, stale detail request concurrency, synchronous full-history transcript processing, and unbounded preview cache publication.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
